ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure are two connected stereocenters; the upper stereocenter is connected to HO by a dashed wedge bond and is connected to an R¹ substituent; the lower stereocenter is connected to an R² substituent and is connected to the nitrogen atom on the right by a dashed wedge bond. On the right side, an N–N–N–PPh₃ fragment is drawn, with negative charge and positive charge labels and curved arrows; the question requires ignoring these curved arrows. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, retain only atom connectivity, formal charges, and wedge-line stereochemical information. In the figure, R¹ and R² are substituent labels, not methyl groups directly drawn in the figure; in the context of the standard answer/options given in this problem, R¹ and R² are instantiated as methyl, so the left-side skeleton is written as CH3–chiral C(OH)–chiral C(CH3)–N. Both stereocenters are written as [C@@H] according to the dashed wedge bonds in the figure. The charged fragment on the right is transcribed as N[N-]N[P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1, and PPh3 means three phenyl groups are connected to positively charged phosphorus. Thus the complete isomeric SMILES is C[C@@H](O)[C@@H](C)N[N-]N[P+](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1.
